applies_why: The judge text gives UNDERDETERMINED for a link dispute, so K-S2's restriction on grounds for UNDERDETERMINED applies.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED: it could bar only an express single-verse-silence rationale for UNDERDETERMINED, or it could bar any UNDERDETERMINED where no chain compels.
why: The judge rests UNDERDETERMINED on the two chains not forcing each other, not on any single verse's failure to state the link or its contrary, so K-S2 is not violated.
